We currently have no evidence of life beyond Earth. Whether life exists elsewhere in the universe is one of the most profound questions of all time. The answer will change our understanding of existence forever, whether it reveals a universe abundant with life, one where life is rare and fragile, or even a universe devoid of life altogether. 
The quest for answers not only seeks to uncover extraterrestrial life but also sheds light on our own place in the universe—how we came to be, how life originated, and perhaps where we are headed. 
Interestingly, we don't have a universally accepted definition of life itself. However, we may not actually need one. We only need to detect the telltale signs of life in the atmosphere of an exoplanet, and we already have a better understanding of what those signs look like here on Earth.

history.content: Explain the differences between Astronomy and Astrology.

Astronomy is the scientific study of everything in outer space. Astronomers and other scientists study stars, galaxies, and other celestial objects, using evidence and data to understand how the universe was made, what else is out there, and how we fit in. On the other hand, astrology is not a science. It is based on the belief that the location of certain stars and planets in the sky can predict the future or describe what a person is like. While astrology is important to some cultural traditions, its claims are not based on scientific evidence.
In summary, the main difference between astronomy and astrology is that astronomy is a science that studies the physical universe, while astrology is a belief system that attempts to correlate celestial events with human experiences.

The universe encompasses everything—it includes all of space, as well as all the matter and energy contained within that space. It even encompasses time itself, and, of course, it includes you. The universe contains all the energy and matter that exists. Much of the observable matter in the universe is made up of individual hydrogen atoms, which are the simplest atomic elements. A hydrogen atom consists of just a proton and an electron; if the atom also contains a neutron, it is known as deuterium.
NASA states that the universe is about 13.8 billion years old.
Is it impossible to determine its exact age?

A galaxy is a grouping of stars, and almost all the stars in the universe exist within galaxies. A galaxy is a vast collection of gas, dust, billions of stars, and their solar systems, all held together by gravity.
 Some galaxies are spiral-shaped, with curved arms that resemble pinwheels. Other galaxies are smooth and oval-shaped, known as elliptical galaxies. Additionally, there are galaxies with irregular shapes that look like blobs. The light we see from each of these galaxies comes from the stars within them.
In which galaxy is the planet Earth located?
The planet Earth is located in the Milky Way galaxy.
